summary: jenscolt's body (the top shell) as one parametric build123d solid in jenscolt's frame: an outer skin lofted from 8 superellipse control sections up the vertical spine, a wall cut by an inner skin derived from the same table, and every visible detail a named feature placed on it; nothing moves.

parts.name: body
parts.role: the spider's top shell: skin, wall open at the rim, eye block with the two big eye bores and knurled rings, nose plate, two small eye tubes, chin arch and bridge, side scoops, side panel lines, rear lip, rear tab, two screw bosses
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh (spideybot_body); N1 form part, not printed

options: a loft of 8 horizontal superellipse control sections (half-width, front / back half-lengths, front / back exponents) up the vertical spine x = CX, PCHIP-interpolated in z
a table of measured sections (a mesh copy)
alternatives.choice: a loft of 8 horizontal superellipse control sections (half-width, front / back half-lengths, front / back exponents) up the vertical spine x = CX, PCHIP-interpolated in z
alternatives.why: 40 readable numbers that a person can change; a measured table cannot be edited

options: an OCCT offset of the lofted skin
an inner skin lofted from the same control table, each meridian eroded by the wall, cut from the outer one
alternatives.choice: an inner skin lofted from the same control table, each meridian eroded by the wall, cut from the outer one
alternatives.why: the offset of the loft ran over 4 min without finishing; the inner loft takes under a second and keeps WALL one parameter

acceptance.text: one valid closed build123d solid, exported by build.py to out/body.stl and out/body.step in jenscolt's frame at 100 %
build.py --sweep rebuilds at S 0.65 and with the wall and the section scale at 0.8x and 1.2x, and prints FAIL for any variant that is not one valid closed solid
fidelity of the body to spideybot_body.stl as a viewer above and around sees it: p95 ≤ 2.0 mm and max ≤ 4.0 mm both ways (the default)
the visible details present as shape: big eye sockets with knurled rings, small eyes, nose plate, chin arch, side scoops, panel lines, rear lip and tab
every shape parameter at the top of build.py with its source (a probe or a section); the shape comes from parameters, not from the mesh
acceptance.note: code review by the coordinator: the judge sees pictures, not code

acceptance.text: outer form and wall thickness separate parameters (wall as an inward offset of the skin)
acceptance.note: SKIN_CTRL is the outer form, WALL the wall: the inner skin is the same table eroded by WALL (an OCCT offset of the loft hangs)

acceptance.text: every visible detail a named feature placed on the skin: eye sockets and rings, front grille, panel lines, rear features
not build.py reads a mesh: the reference meshes are read only by the gates and the designer's probes
the default fidelity gate passes, the sweep's variants are valid solids, and the judge scores ≥ 0.70 against the mesh

diagram: SKIN_CTRL (8 sections, 40 numbers) --loft--> outer skin; same table eroded by WALL --loft--> inner skin; outer - inner = shell open at Z_RIM; + eye block, rings, nose, small eyes, bridge, scoops, rear lip, tab, bosses; - bores, chin arch, boss holes, panel lines
